accepted.s: As per APSES 2025-26, the number of farmers practising natural farming in Andhra Pradesh is
accepted.x: APSES 2025-26 records 10.20 lakh farmers practising natural farming in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the current coverage figure from older and national farmer counts.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the area and number of Gram Panchayats covered under natural farming in Andhra Pradesh as per APSES 2025-26?
accepted.x: The reported coverage is 4.89 lakh hectares and 4,116 Gram Panchayats.
accepted.tq: Match two related numerical indicators without confusing area with kitchen-garden coverage.

accepted.s: The number of NF kitchen gardens reported under the natural farming programme is

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the targets of natural farming in Andhra Pradesh:
1. All Gram Panchayats are targeted to be covered by 2026-27.
2. The target for 2028-29 is 41 lakh farmers on 19 lakh hectares.
3. The targets are associated with the Swarna Andhra@2047 initiative.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: universal Gram Panchayat coverage is targeted for 2026-27, while 41 lakh farmers and 19 lakh hectares are targeted for 2028-29 under Swarna Andhra@2047.
accepted.tq: Test multiple target years and figures together through coded statements.
accepted.sec: Coverage and targets - farmers, villages, area, universal coverage target year  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The natural farming programme works in clusters generally consisting of
accepted.x: The programme works in clusters of five villages covering approximately 1,500 to 2,500 acres.
accepted.tq: Recall a paired structural figure by linking the number of villages with the acreage range.
accepted.sec: Coverage and targets - farmers, villages, area, universal coverage target year  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Under the 2024-25 plan, which one of the following correctly describes the proposed cluster arrangement per Parliamentary Constituency?
o: 10-15 village clusters, 5,000 acres per constituency and 50,000 acres in total
5-10 village clusters, 1,000 acres per constituency and 25,000 acres in total
2-5 village clusters, 2,500 acres per constituency and 10,000 acres in total
5-10 village clusters, 25,000 acres per constituency and 1,000 acres in total
accepted.x: The 2024-25 plan adopts 5-10 village clusters per Parliamentary Constituency, with 1,000 acres per constituency and 25,000 acres in total as stated in the programme design.
accepted.tq: Detect the reversed numerical relationship between per-constituency and total coverage figures.
accepted.sec: Coverage and targets - farmers, villages, area, universal coverage target year  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The earlier count cited for farmers covered under the natural farming programme was

accepted.s: Rythu Sadhikara Samstha, commonly abbreviated as RySS, is
o: a private company established by farmer producer organisations
a not-for-profit company set up by the Department of Agriculture, Government of Andhra Pradesh
a statutory corporation under the Finance Department
a cooperative society under the Panchayat Raj Department
accepted.x: RySS stands for Rythu Sadhikara Samstha and is a not-for-profit company established by the Department of Agriculture, Government of Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Use the full-form and institutional-nature combination to avoid confusing a company with a statutory body or cooperative.
accepted.sec: Implementing agency RySS - full form, nature, incorporation year, parent department  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: RySS was incorporated in
accepted.x: Rythu Sadhikara Samstha was incorporated in October 2014.
accepted.tq: Test the exact incorporation month and year against nearby programme dates.
accepted.sec: Implementing agency RySS - full form, nature, incorporation year, parent department  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: In the context of Zero Budget Natural Farming, the expression “zero budget” primarily refers to
o: cultivation without purchased fertilisers or pesticides
accepted.x: “Zero budget” refers to avoiding purchased fertilisers and pesticides; it does not mean that every input or labour cost is absent.
accepted.tq: Interpret the exact meaning of a potentially misleading programme label.
accepted.sec: ZBNF proponent and rebranding to APCNF  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Andhra Pradesh launched ZBNF in 2016 and subsequently renamed it as
accepted.x: The programme launched as ZBNF in 2016 was renamed APCNF, meaning Andhra Pradesh Community-managed Natural Farming.
accepted.tq: Test the exact expansion of a renamed programme rather than a similar-sounding agricultural term.
accepted.sec: ZBNF proponent and rebranding to APCNF  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Jeevamrutham — seed treatment with cow dung, cow urine and lime
Mulching — sowing before rains on residual moisture
accepted.x: Ghanajeevamrutham is the solid form of Jeevamrutham. Beejamrutham is the seed treatment, while mulching is the use of crop residue or straw cover.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure practice-definition pair and reject swapped meanings.
accepted.sec: APCNF practices  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Beejamrutham is used as
o: a solid bio-fertiliser made only from straw
a seed treatment prepared with cow dung, cow urine and lime
a trap crop consisting of marigold and castor
a crop-residue cover for suppressing weeds
accepted.x: Beejamrutham is a seed treatment involving cow dung, cow urine and lime.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a named preparation from other APCNF practices by its specific use.
accepted.sec: APCNF practices  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following ingredients are associated with Jeevamrutham?
1. Cow dung
2. Cow urine
3. Jaggery
4. Pulse flour
5. Soil
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Jeevamrutham is prepared from cow dung, cow urine, jaggery, pulse flour and soil.
accepted.tq: Test a complete ingredient list through an all-inclusive coded option.
accepted.sec: APCNF practices  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about APCNF practices:
1. Mulching uses crop-residue or straw cover to conserve moisture and suppress weeds.
2. Pre-Monsoon Dry Sowing involves sowing before the rains on residual moisture.
3. PMDS is associated with millets, pulses and oilseeds.
4. A 365-day green cover is maintained through cover cropping and polyculture.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe mulching, PMDS and the 365-day green-cover approach.
accepted.tq: Combine closely related practice definitions while checking each statement independently.
accepted.sec: APCNF practices  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT associated with the APCNF practice package?
o: Exclusive dependence on purchased chemical fertilisers
Trap crops such as marigold and castor
accepted.x: APCNF promotes native seeds, minimal or no tillage, livestock integration and trap crops; exclusive dependence on purchased chemical fertilisers is contrary to the model.
accepted.tq: Find the one option that reverses the underlying principle of the programme.
accepted.sec: APCNF practices  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Kurnool is promoting Pre-Monsoon Dry Sowing on approximately how much area because of the El Nino-related rain deficit?
accepted.x: Kurnool is promoting PMDS on 92,000 acres in response to the El Nino-related rain deficit.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact area figure associated with a district-specific initiative.
accepted.sec: APCNF practices  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Food Planet Prize 2026:
1. APCNF was the first Indian finalist.
2. The prize amount was 1.5 million US dollars.
3. The award was associated with the Curt Bergfors Foundation.
4. It was held at Bastad in Sweden in June 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct: APCNF was the first Indian finalist, and the June 2026 prize at Bastad, Sweden, carried an award of 1.5 million US dollars from the Curt Bergfors Foundation.
accepted.tq: Verify a named international award through its amount, sponsor, place and finalist status.
accepted.sec: Outcomes and evaluations - yield, cost, income, international awards  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following outcomes has been observed in the field in relation to APCNF?
1. Crop diversity
2. Better soil health
3. Higher incomes
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Field observations associated with APCNF include crop diversity, improved soil health and higher incomes.
accepted.tq: Use an all-correct option for a compact list of reported outcomes.
accepted.sec: Outcomes and evaluations - yield, cost, income, international awards  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the international spread of the APCNF model?
o: It is being replicated only within Andhra Pradesh.
It has been replicated only in Kenya and Sweden.
It is restricted to the five-village clusters of Andhra Pradesh.
It is being replicated in other Indian States, Zambia and Sri Lanka.
accepted.x: The APCNF model is being replicated in other States of India as well as in Zambia and Sri Lanka.
accepted.tq: Test the geographical extent of replication against restrictive alternatives.
